instructions: The night before: in a large bowl, stir the flour, salt, sugar and yeast. Make a well in the middle and pour in the olive oil. Knead while slowly adding 1/2 cup lukewarm water, for about 5 minutes, until the dough is smooth, stretchy and no longer sticky. Cover it with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight. If you didn't make it ahead, let the dough rest on the counter for 30 minutes instead.
In the morning, take the dough out of the fridge and leave it on the counter for 20 minutes. Crumble the feta into a bowl.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll each into a circle about 1/4 inch thick, sized to fit your frying pan.
Spread the feta over two of the circles, leaving the edge bare. Cover each with a second circle and press the edges together with a fork. Seal them well so the feta doesn't leak into the pan.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Add 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil to coat the bottom.
Fry one stuffed round for about 3 minutes, until the underside is golden. Flip it and fry for about 3 minutes, until the other side is golden.
Transfer it to paper towels. Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan and fry the second round the same way.
Cut each round into 4 wedges and serve warm.
advance_prep_notes: Make the dough the night before and refrigerate it
method_notes: Cook with Renu (the lead by the 20 rating rule) and My Greek Dish use the same plain yeast dough with olive oil, rolled thin and fried with crumbled feta sealed between two circles. Katerina's Kouzina adds herbs and honey, which are left out here. Both rest the dough for 30 minutes at room temperature; resting it overnight in the fridge is Pomona's adaptation so the morning is only rolling, filling and frying, about 25 minutes. The sources give no frying times, so the 3 minutes a side is a cue to check by colour.
